mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day pre-trigger average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which tends to boost investor confidence and drive positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: In 20 post-trigger days, SPX 20-day returns show no significant deviation from the prior 30-day mean (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 2% for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as it signals robust economic momentum and demand for equity risk assets.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 106.5 for two consecutive months (as of current month's value)
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, cumulative SPX 20-day returns are negative and statistically indistinguishable from a flat trend (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to turn negative due to anticipated rate hikes that reduce the present value of future cash flows.
failure_condition: In 20 post-trigger days, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day pre-trigger mean (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the M2 money supply (not directly observable in the catalog, but proxy via FEDFUNDS falling > 4.0% in a month) predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return due to tightened liquidity and higher risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls by > 4.0 percentage points in a month
failure_condition: Over the 60-day window, SPX 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative across 4 consecutive windows of 15 days each (average p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% triggers a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as it signals labor market strength and reduced recession risk.
failure_condition: In the following 5 days, SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (not directly observable; proxy via HOUST) show a month-on-month increase of at least 5% and industrial production (INDPRO) is above 108, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive due to dual demand signals.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% and INDPRO > 108 for the same month
failure_condition: Across 10 consecutive 20-day windows following the trigger, cumulative SPX 20-day returns are negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a period of declining consumer sentiment (proxy via GDPC1 quarterly decline > 10%) and rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 260), the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to deflationary and inflationary pressures both depressing growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarter-on-quarter < -10% and CPIAUCSL > 260 in the same quarter
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, SPX 20-day returns are not consistently negative across 3 non-overlapping 20-day periods (average p > 0.10).
